classification_note: The ARVO metadata leaves this sample unclassified, but the saved sanitizer trace and reproduction report both show an AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow read in `md_is_container_mark`, so this GT classifies it as CWE-125.

bug_description.original:
A buffer overflow occurs on input in c-string format such as:
"
# h1
c  hh##e2ked

 A | rong__ ___strong ������\a����
# h1
h# #2
### h3
#### h4��������\
##### h5
#*#####�
6"
bug_description.normalized: The staged 9-byte witness `20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 31` is handled by `fuzz-mdhtml` as two 4-byte flag words plus a 1-byte Markdown document. After the harness consumes the first 8 bytes as `parser_flags` and `renderer_flags`, `md_parse()` stores `ctx.text` on the final byte `'1'` and `ctx.size == 1`. `md_process_doc()` analyzes that only line, `md_analyze_line()` routes it into `md_is_container_mark()`, and ordered-list detection clamps `max_end` to `ctx->size`, scans the lone digit, and advances `off` from 0 to 1. The vulnerable `if(off > beg && (CH(off) == '.' || CH(off) == ')') && ...)` then probes `CH(off)` without first proving `off < ctx->size`, so it dereferences `ctx->text[1]` one byte past the end of the original 9-byte testcase allocation. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 at `src/md4c.c:5659`, and the patch fixes this exact obligation by adding `off < ctx->size` before the delimiter test.

evidence_note: No `trace_feedback.json` was present, and `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so this Stage 02 pass remained fully source-grounded. The saved ASan trace, exact vulnerable source, and staged one-line patch were sufficient to close the chain without extra instrumentation.

source.description: First non-harness project statement that materializes the parser-visible input span. After the harness consumes its two 4-byte flag words, md4c stores a pointer to the remaining Markdown slice and its length in `ctx`.
source.value_from: The staged PoC at `gt_results/arvo_31332/poc` has sha256 `e6eeb4cb3a8d11c59199e56f464167953c92287f81b801f18f0b43dbc83ff1e4` and exact bytes `20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 31`. `fuzz-mdhtml` reads the first 4 bytes as `parser_flags == 0x20202020` and the next 4 bytes as `renderer_flags == 0x20202020`, then calls `md_html()` / `md_parse()` with `text` pointing at the final byte `0x31 ('1')` and `size == 1`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.code:
if(off > beg  &&
       (CH(off) == _T('.') || CH(off) == _T(')'))  &&
       (off+1 >= ctx->size || ISBLANK(off+1) || ISNEWLINE(off+1)))
root_cause.description: After ordered-list digit scanning advances `off` to the end of the document, this condition checks only `off > beg` before dereferencing `CH(off)` to look for `'.'` or `')'`. When the digit run reaches the document boundary, `off == ctx->size`, so the delimiter probe itself is out of bounds. The patch fixes this exact obligation by inserting `off < ctx->size` before `CH(off)`.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `CH(off)` expands to `ctx->text[(off)]`; with `ctx.text` pointing at the final byte of the 9-byte testcase allocation and `off == 1`, this expression reads the first byte past that allocation.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `src/md4c.c:5659:9`, on an address 0 bytes to the right of the 9-byte region allocated for the testcase by libFuzzer.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is the first point where the attacker-controlled markdown subspan becomes parser state. For the staged witness, `ctx.text` points at the single remaining payload byte `'1'` and `ctx.size` becomes 1, the bound later violated by `CH(off)` after `off` advances to the end of that slice.

parser_admitted.description: For the parser-visible one-byte line, indentation analysis yields `line->indent == 0`, so `md_analyze_line()` takes the new-container path and dispatches to `md_is_container_mark()` before any later line-type checks.

fine_trace.note: Stores the parser-visible document span. For the staged witness, the harness has already consumed the first 8 bytes as flags, so `ctx.text` points at the final byte `'1'` inside the original 9-byte testcase allocation and `ctx.size` becomes the remaining length 1.

`md_line_indentation()` tests the first parser-visible byte with `ISBLANK(off)`. Because `ctx.text[0]` is `'1'`, not blank, it returns 0, leaves `off == 0`, and records `line->beg == 0` for the only line.

With `line->indent == 0` and `ctx->code_indent_offset == 4`, the new-container branch is taken and `md_analyze_line()` calls `md_is_container_mark()` with `beg == off == 0` to test whether the line starts a list or quote marker.

Ordered-list detection clamps `max_end` to `ctx->size`, so here `max_end == 1`. The loop sees the lone byte `'1'` as a digit, sets `p_container->start` to 1, and advances `off` from 0 to 1, exactly to the end of the markdown slice.

fine_trace.code:
if(off > beg  &&
       (CH(off) == _T('.') || CH(off) == _T(')'))  &&
       (off+1 >= ctx->size || ISBLANK(off+1) || ISNEWLINE(off+1)))
fine_trace.note: Root cause. After step 4, `off > beg` is true and `off == ctx->size == 1`, but this condition has no `off < ctx->size` conjunct before the delimiter probe. Evaluating the `CH(off)` arm therefore treats the one-past-end cursor as if it still pointed inside the document.

Sink. `CH(off)` expands to `ctx->text[(off)]`; with `ctx.text` at the final byte of the original 9-byte testcase allocation and `off == 1`, this dereferences the first byte beyond that allocation. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting heap-buffer-overflow read at this expression, with stack `md_is_container_mark -> md_analyze_line -> md_process_doc`.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: n/a: the overread is on libFuzzer's testcase allocation; the patch-targeted missing bound is inside `md_is_container_mark`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `docker exec gt-arvo_31332-workspace /bin/bash -lc '/bin/arvo run'`, which fed the staged `poc` to `/out/fuzz-mdhtml` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `md_is_container_mark` with stack `md_analyze_line -> md_process_doc -> md_parse`.

format.name: 9-byte fuzz-mdhtml witness
format.contract: Exactly 9 bytes `20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 31`. `fuzz-mdhtml` interprets the first 4 bytes as `parser_flags == 0x20202020`, the next 4 bytes as `renderer_flags == 0x20202020`, and passes the final byte `0x31 ('1')` to `md_html()` as the entire Markdown document. In the staged vulnerable source, that one-byte document makes ordered-list parsing advance `off` to `ctx->size == 1` and then probe `CH(off)` for `'.'` or `')'`, triggering the observed overread.
